note: 1911 household schedules from the Newcastle Drive gap round and the streets it ran into, read from the images supplied by A. Hagues. Newcastle Drive 1, 3, 11, 13, 15, 17, 21, and 23 to 37 which the covers give as 6 to 16 Pelham Terrace, converted by the rule the record already holds: Newcastle Drive number = 39 minus the Pelham Terrace number, for the even side. Also Park Lodge on Park Row, 1 Huntingdon Drive, an unnumbered Huntingdon Drive household and 5 Lenton Road. Everyone the record already holds is bound by number, several of them under a spelling their own hand disagrees with. Six Castle Grove households are included and none of them can be filed: the property list holds 4, 5, 6, 6a and 7 only, and the covers give 1, 2 and four with no number at all.

people.bio: American lawyer, politician and diplomat. A Republican, he sat in the Ohio House of Representatives from 1888 and was Ohio Secretary of State from 1893 to 1897, serving under Governor William McKinley and his successor Asa Bushnell. McKinley, as President, appointed him to the consular service, and he spent the rest of his working life abroad: consul at Glasgow 1897-1906, at Callao in Peru 1906-1910, at Nottingham 1910-1911 and at Birmingham from 1913. He was educated at Ohio Wesleyan University and the Cincinnati Law School. He died of influenza at Birmingham while still in post, and is buried at Urbana, Ohio.
